financials_interim.notes: Union Assurance PLC (UAL) -- single-entity Company filing (no Group/Company split; UAL's own controlling entity is John Keells Holdings PLC, but UAL itself has no consolidated subsidiaries in this filing), stored as one GROUP-basis row per this project's single-entity-filer convention (AAIC/JINS/AINS precedent). Uses the SIX-MONTH CUMULATIVE 'For the period ended 30 June' statements (Income Statement p.2, Balance Sheet p.6, Cash Flow p.9), not the separately-disclosed 'For the Quarter ended 30 June' Q2-only statements on p.4-5, consistent with AAIC/JINS/AINS precedent. FIELD MAPPING (insurer convention per task guidance): revenue = the filing's own 'Total net revenue' subtotal (19,657,449 vs 17,657,718 LY) = Net written premium (12,399,195 = GWP 13,389,768 less premium ceded to reinsurers 990,573) + Total other revenue (7,258,254 = Net investment income 6,875,124 + Net realised gain/(loss) (84,887) + Net fair value gains 458,148 + Other income 9,869) -- the insurer's own disclosed top-line, materially the task's prescribed 'Net Earned Premium + Investment/Other Income' concept. operating_profit = the filing's own 'Profit from operations' line (723,879 vs 907,565 LY) -- UAL's P&L DOES disclose a clean operating-profit subtotal before 'Share of results of equity accounted investee' and PBT, unlike AAIC/JINS which had no such line. finance_costs/finance_income left BLANK: no separate finance-cost/finance-income P&L line exists (Interest paid of Rs.28,832k appears only in the cash-flow statement, not as a face P&L line); investment income is presented as part of Total other revenue, not as a distinct finance-income line, consistent with AAIC/JINS precedent. depreciation_amortization = 319,735 (P&L face line, vs 368,408 LY). minority_interest left blank (no NCI, wholly single-entity). MATERIAL DRIVER: 'Share of results of equity accounted investee, net of tax' fell 100% to NIL in H1 2026 from Rs.170,818k in H1 2025 (confirmed by segment note 6 and by the 'Transaction with Associates' related-party note showing a zero receivable/payable balance in both years) -- this single line accounts for Rs.170,818k of the Rs.354,504k PBT decline (48.2% of it) on its own, i.e. nearly half of the profit fall is simply the disappearance of an associate income contribution that existed a year ago, not a deterioration in UAL's own insurance operations. The remaining Rs.183,686k of the PBT decline (-20.2% at the 'Profit from operations' line) is driven by Total benefits, claims and expenses growing 13.0% to Rs.18,933,570k (from Rs.16,750,153k), outpacing Total net revenue growth of 11.3% (to Rs.19,657,449k from Rs.17,657,718k); within that, Change in insurance contract liabilities (the life fund reserve build-up) rose 17.1% to Rs.9,319,703k from Rs.7,963,481k, alone adding Rs.1,356,222k of cost, more than the entire revenue growth of Rs.1,999,731k on a net basis once other expense lines are added. Also notable: Net realised gain/(loss) on investments swung from a Rs.305,794k GAIN to an Rs.84,887k LOSS (a Rs.390,681k negative swing), partly offset by Net investment income growing a healthy 16.0% to Rs.6,875,124k. Balance sheet is liquidity-ordered (no current/non-current split) -- current_assets/current_liabilities left BLANK per AAIC/JINS/AINS precedent. inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left BLANK per the task's insurer guidance: closest analogues are Premiums receivable (1,104,071) and Reinsurance receivable (514,024) on the asset side, and Reinsurance payables (633,274) and Other liabilities (6,850,787) on the liability side -- all insurance-specific, not generic trade items, excluded rather than force-mapped. cash_and_equivalents = balance sheet 'Cash in hand and at bank' (1,491,663) -- NOTE this is the gross BS figure; the cash-flow statement's own Note B nets this against a Rs.187,512k bank overdraft to a narrower Rs.1,304,151k closing cash-and-equivalents figure, consistent with the AAIC precedent of storing the gross BS cash line. short_term_borrowings = Bank overdraft (187,512), the only short-term-debt-like line disclosed (no separate loans/borrowings line exists on this BS at all); long_term_borrowings left BLANK -- the only other debt-like item is Lease liabilities (545,495), treated as an operating-lease obligation rather than borrowings per the AINS precedent, not a bank loan/debenture. capex = 262,241 (Purchase of PP&E 171,906 + Purchase of intangible assets 90,335, cash flow statement; proceeds from PPE disposal of 1,926 kept separate, not netted). cash_from_operations = 8,049,413; cash_from_investing = (5,186,669); cash_from_financing = (3,057,660). shares_in_issue = 589,285,720 (Note 20, Stated Capital; unchanged since 31 Dec 2025). Identity/cross-checks all tie exactly: PBT-tax=PAT (723,879-219,640=504,239); EPS = PAT/shares = 504,239,000/589,285,720 = Rs.0.8556, rounds to disclosed 0.86; Net assets per share = Total equity/shares = 19,090,376,000/589,285,720 = Rs.32.40, ties exactly to disclosed Note 19 figure; Total assets=Total liabilities+Total equity (131,523,135=112,432,759+19,090,376) ties exactly. Total equity fell sharply (19,090,376 vs 23,372,593 at FYE 2025) mainly due to a Rs.2,946,429k final dividend paid for 2025 and a Rs.1,858,337k other-comprehensive-income loss (fair value reserve on AFS assets and the related insurance-liability shadow-accounting adjustment), not from the period's own trading loss.

interim_updates.note_text: Union Assurance PLC (UAL) reported Total Net Revenue of Rs.19,657.45mn for the six months ended 30 June 2026, +11.3% YoY (H1 2025: Rs.17,657.72mn), but Profit from Operations fell 20.2% to Rs.723.88mn (H1 2025: Rs.907.57mn), Profit before Tax fell 32.9% to Rs.723.88mn (H1 2025: Rs.1,078.38mn), and Profit for the Period fell 37.2% to Rs.504.24mn (H1 2025: Rs.802.999mn); Basic EPS fell to Rs.0.86 from Rs.1.36. The Rs.354.50mn PBT decline decomposes exactly into two pieces: (1) 'Share of results of equity accounted investee, net of tax' fell 100% to NIL from Rs.170.82mn in H1 2025 (segment note 6 and the related-party note both confirm no associate income this period) -- a Rs.170.82mn swing that is 48.2% of the entire PBT decline on its own, and is unrelated to UAL's core insurance trading; (2) Profit from Operations itself fell Rs.183.69mn (-20.2%), because Total Benefits, Claims and Expenses grew 13.0% to Rs.18,933.57mn (from Rs.16,750.15mn) faster than Total Net Revenue's 11.3% growth -- within this, Change in Insurance Contract Liabilities (the life fund reserve build-up) rose 17.1% to Rs.9,319.70mn from Rs.7,963.48mn, adding Rs.1,356.22mn of cost on its own. Gross Written Premium grew a healthy 15.0% to Rs.13,389.77mn (from Rs.11,604.83mn) and Net Investment Income grew 16.0% to Rs.6,875.12mn, so the underlying insurance and investment-income engines were both growing; the profit decline instead reflects (a) the one-off loss of an equity-accounted associate's income contribution and (b) a faster-growing life insurance reserve liability that a 15% premium increase alone did not keep pace with, compounded by Net Realised Gain/(Loss) swinging from a Rs.305.79mn GAIN to an Rs.84.89mn LOSS (a Rs.390.68mn negative swing) on the investment portfolio. Income Tax Expense fell 20.2% YoY to Rs.219.64mn, tracking the smaller pretax profit base almost exactly proportionally.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is UAL's first financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB (the filing discloses six-month cumulative 'For the period ended 30 June' figures on p.2-3 and Q2-only 'For the Quarter ended 30 June' figures separately on p.4-5, consistent with the AAIC/JINS/AINS precedent of using the six-month cumulative statements, so no independently-derived Q1-2026 figure exists in this DB to build a QoQ split). Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) the identity and nature of the equity-accounted investee whose income contribution fell to nil is not named anywhere in this interim filing (it is referenced only via the generic P&L line and the 'Transaction with Associates' related-party note, which shows a zero receivable/payable balance and a token Rs.171k prior-year services transaction -- no explanation is given for why the associate contribution disappeared, e.g. disposal, dilution, or the associate itself reporting nil/negative results); (2) no breakdown is given of which asset classes drove the Rs.390.68mn swing in Net Realised Gain/(Loss) from a gain to a loss (equity vs. government securities vs. corporate debt); (3) operating_margin/net_margin are mathematically well-defined here (both revenue and profit stayed positive throughout) so no distortion caveat is needed, unlike some NBFI/treasury entries in this DB.
interim_updates.takeaway: UAL's 37.2% PAT decline is not a core-underwriting story -- Gross Written Premium grew a healthy 15.0% and Net Investment Income grew 16.0% -- but reflects (1) the one-off loss of an equity-accounted associate's income contribution (Rs.170.82mn to NIL, 48.2% of the PBT decline alone) and (2) the life insurance reserve liability (Change in Insurance Contract Liabilities, +17.1% to Rs.9,319.70mn) growing faster than premium income, compounded by a swing from realised investment gains to realised losses. Total equity's sharp fall to Rs.19,090.38mn (from Rs.23,372.59mn) is a dividend-and-OCI story, not a trading-result story, since profit for the period was still positive at Rs.504.24mn.

operational_highlights: Total Net Revenue Rs.19,657.45mn, +11.3% YoY; Profit from Operations Rs.723.88mn, -20.2% YoY; PBT Rs.723.88mn, -32.9% YoY; PAT Rs.504.24mn, -37.2% YoY; Basic EPS Rs.0.86 vs Rs.1.36 PY.
Share of results of equity accounted investee fell 100% to NIL from Rs.170.82mn in H1 2025 -- 48.2% of the entire Rs.354.50mn PBT decline on its own, per segment note 6 and the related-party note.

Change in Insurance Contract Liabilities (life fund reserve build-up) rose 17.1% to Rs.9,319.70mn from Rs.7,963.48mn, adding Rs.1,356.22mn of cost and outpacing the 15.0% GWP growth to Rs.13,389.77mn.
Net Realised Gain/(Loss) on investments swung from a Rs.305.79mn gain to an Rs.84.89mn loss (Rs.390.68mn negative swing), while Net Investment Income itself grew a healthy 16.0% to Rs.6,875.12mn.

Total equity fell to Rs.19,090.38mn from Rs.23,372.59mn at FYE 2025, mainly a Rs.2,946.43mn final dividend paid for 2025 and a Rs.1,858.34mn other-comprehensive-income loss on the AFS fair value reserve, not the period's trading result.
key_drivers: Disappearance of the equity-accounted associate's income contribution (Rs.170.82mn in H1 2025 to NIL in H1 2026) accounts for 48.2% of the entire PBT decline on its own -- a one-off, non-operating item.

Change in Insurance Contract Liabilities (life fund reserve) grew 17.1% to Rs.9,319.70mn, outpacing 15.0% GWP growth and 11.3% Total Net Revenue growth -- the core driver of the remaining operating-profit decline.

Net Realised Gain/(Loss) on the investment portfolio swung Rs.390.68mn unfavourably (a Rs.305.79mn gain to an Rs.84.89mn loss), a secondary drag partly offset by 16.0% growth in Net Investment Income.
